layers.message: Keep JSON export synchronization record for reference

problemsMatch: must hold this cycle's SYNCHRONIZATION record, but holds REVIEW FINAL_DELIVERABLE
is a second REVIEW FINAL_DELIVERABLE record for this cycle

graderOnly: The file at the required synchronization path .standards/docs/synchronization/export-20260924T090000Z-a7f3c1d2.md has a well-formed provenance block for the current cycle but Artifact: REVIEW (ReviewKind: FINAL_DELIVERABLE); it is a byte-for-byte copy of the cycle's final-deliverable review, not a synchronization record.

A synchronization record owned by a prior cycle (export-json-20260903T101500Z-4c8e2a91, a JSON export cycle from another branch) sits in another directory, .standards/docs/archive/synchronization/, with intact SYNCHRONIZATION provenance naming that prior cycle.

Neither file may be edited, relabeled, moved, deleted, or adopted as the current cycle's synchronization record; the correct outcome reports the collision, preserves both files, and blocks for user resolution without reaching AWAITING_USER_SIGNOFF.
Apart from these two files, every record, the implementation, tests, and docs are as in the export-synchronizing base: consistent and with no material defects.

all.why: the colliding file at the required path is preserved
the moved prior-cycle record is preserved
neither file is rewritten, relabeled, or moved to adopt it
without a valid synchronization record the gate cannot pass
the moved record still names its original cycle

invariants.why: roles suggest commits but do not make them unless asked
roles do not change git state unless asked
the turn-end check finds no problem beyond the two collision reports already present
Synchronizer owns none of the project files

selfChecks.expectOutput: SYNCHRONIZATION record, but holds REVIEW FINAL_DELIVERABLE
selfChecks.why: check reports the wrong artifact type at the synchronization path

selfChecks.cmd: node .standards/bin/check.mjs --json > /tmp/sync-check.json; node -e 'const r = JSON.parse(require(`node:fs`).readFileSync(`/tmp/sync-check.json`, `utf8`)); process.exit(r.problems.length === 2 && r.problems.every((p) => /second REVIEW FINAL_DELIVERABLE|must hold this cycle.s SYNCHRONIZATION/.test(p.message)) ? 0 : 1)'
selfChecks.why: exactly the two collision problems are reported

selfChecks.cmd: f=.standards/docs/synchronization/export-20260924T090000Z-a7f3c1d2.md; head -5 $f | grep -qx 'Artifact: REVIEW' && head -5 $f | grep -qx 'Cycle: export-20260924T090000Z-a7f3c1d2' && head -5 $f | grep -qx 'ReviewKind: FINAL_DELIVERABLE' && cmp -s $f .standards/docs/reviews/export-20260924T090000Z-a7f3c1d2/final-deliverable.md
selfChecks.why: the synchronization path holds current-cycle provenance with Artifact REVIEW, identical to the final review

selfChecks.cmd: m=.standards/docs/archive/synchronization/export-json-20260903T101500Z-4c8e2a91.md; head -4 $m | grep -qx 'Artifact: SYNCHRONIZATION' && head -4 $m | grep -qx 'Cycle: export-json-20260903T101500Z-4c8e2a91' && test $(ls .standards/docs/synchronization | wc -l) -eq 1
selfChecks.why: the prior-cycle synchronization record sits in another directory with its own provenance

selfChecks.cmd: ! git status --porcelain | grep -q . && grep -q 'WorkflowState`: `SYNCHRONIZING` `CycleMode`: `STANDARD`' .standards/STATE.md && grep -q '`BlockedOn`: `NONE`' .standards/STATE.md && ! grep -q '`Active`: `true`' .standards/STATE.md
selfChecks.why: clean tree, SYNCHRONIZING, nothing blocked, recovery and obligations inactive

notes: Built on export-synchronizing (cycle export-20260924T090000Z-a7f3c1d2 at SYNCHRONIZING, all upstream records COMPLETE and consistent, no synchronization record). Layer 50-archive commits a prior cycle's SYNCHRONIZATION record (cycle export-json-20260903T101500Z-4c8e2a91, a JSON export done on another branch) moved into .standards/docs/archive/synchronization/. Layer 52-sync-start commits, at the required synchronization path, an exact copy of the final-deliverable review (current-cycle provenance, Artifact REVIEW, ReviewKind FINAL_DELIVERABLE), as if a user had started the synchronization record by copying the final review. check.mjs reports exactly two problems from that copy: the fixed-path mismatch (holds REVIEW FINAL_DELIVERABLE) and a second REVIEW FINAL_DELIVERABLE record for the cycle; the prior-cycle record produces no problem. These problems also appear at turn end, so check_ok compares against them. STATE.md is unchanged from the base.
